title: Windowed STFT buckets and FFT-boundary artefacts
summary: A 4096-sample default windowed Fourier transform with quarter-hop overlap applies complementary odd/even masks locally, avoiding full-clip circular ringing. Its output has distinct edge and Nyquist semantics from the v0.2 whole-clip FFT method.
invariants: Preserve input channel identity, source sample count and sample rate; never silently downmix.
Keep full-clip FFT and local WOLA methods independently selectable and logged, including frame size, hop, origin and ceiling.
For a full-Nyquist ceiling include its terminal frequency bin; otherwise frequency ceilings are half-open.
Odd and even WOLA outputs sum to the WOLA-bandlimited reference, not necessarily the unfiltered source.
The same utterance may yield different filtered listening experiences without requiring multiple digital sources.
procedure: Window the padded input with periodic sqrt-Hann; FFT by channel and apply binary complementary parity masks.
Inverse FFT, weight with the same synthesis window, overlap-add with window-square normalization and trim the exact source interval.
Compare full-clip FFT and windowed versions on identical synthetic impulse and voiced controls; report ringing and leakage.
Vary frame sizes/phase origins, keep originals and all parameters immutable.

provenance.claim: Executable method reference with synthetic tests; no source/media attribution.
